title: Portable machine profile
description: machine-bootstrap-contract.md §4. A secrets-free, enumerated snapshot of one machine's choices, written by `profile export` and consumed by `profile seed`. The profile is an UNTRUSTED source of interview defaults: it is never configuration to apply, and never an input to any activation or config loader (§4 invariant). Key order here IS the canonical serialization order (§4.1); validated by lib/schema-validate.mjs, whose closed keyword subset means every constraint below is enforced or the schema is rejected. 1.1 (ADR-0048 §2.1) adds the OPTIONAL `statusline_preset` SCALAR — deliberately a bare string, not a field object: §4.6 lets a 1.0 reader ignore an unknown scalar with a warning, while an unknown OBJECT key would refuse the whole document (a nested/custom item shape is exactly the major-bump case §2.1 names).

schema.description: Carries a MINOR, not a bare major, because the §4.1 forward-compat rule turns on it: a newer minor forgives unknown scalar keys, a same-or-older minor does not, and an unknown major is refused outright.

boundary.description: §4.3 guard 2. Part of the schema, not an afterthought: the write is refused unless EVERY flag is false — including performs_network_request, not merely the writes_* trio.

hostname_hash.description: §4.2 — a sha256 prefix, NEVER the raw hostname.

observed.description: Per-host and NEVER flattened (§5): a flat map would collapse a Claude/Codex version divergence. Only Codex carries `disabled` — Claude reports no enabled/disabled state (test #31).

model_effort.description: §4.4 — every value is read from USER-GLOBAL config only, so a repository's policy is never exported as another machine's global default. `scope` is always `machine`.

notify.description: §4.0 — `notify_channel` is NOT an egress channel. `telegram` is not a value here and must never become one; egress lives on a separate axis below, precisely so tracked configuration can never activate egress (ADR-0041 §2c).

value.description: §4.1 — a POSITIVE integer string; the existing validator rejects `0`. The profile uses the validator's own accepted form rather than inventing a second encoding.

egress.description: A SEPARATE axis from notify (§4.0). `profile seed` must not map one onto the other. The credential is never here — only its environment-variable NAME and a required boolean (§4.2).

credential_required.description: §4.1 — true ONLY when declined === false AND channel.value !== null. The exact conditional is enforced in code (a schema cannot express a cross-field implication) and tested.

permissions.description: §4.5 — the STORED enum carries whatever each host accepts, unsafe values included, because a source machine's value is shown as a labelled note and must have a field to live in. Safety grading is a present/seed-side rule, not a second schema field.

statusline_preset.description: 1.1 (ADR-0048 §2.1) — the adopted statusline item set, carried as a SCALAR preset id (the six-item owner set is `agentic-6`). Appended LAST and kept a bare string: canonicalization serializes unknown keys after known ones, so a trailing scalar keeps a 1.0 reader's canonical hash aligned with a 1.1 reader's over the same document, and §4.6 lets the 1.0 reader ignore it with a warning. The preset id names a policy; the canonical item-policy definition itself lives with the statusline adapter, never inline here. Optional (absent from required) — a profile exported before the statusline stage carries null or nothing.

provenance.description: §4.4 — every exported value carries USER-GLOBAL provenance, or it is not exportable. A CLOSED set, not free text: these are the three sources the §4.4 readers actually read — the user config.toml (`user-global`), and egress's env / fail-closed-verified local layer, both of which are user-scope by construction. A label outside this set means a reader nobody vetted for the §4.4 rule, and `repo`/`repo-local` must never appear. `null` accompanies a null value (nothing was found to export).

ruleArray.description: §4.1 — capped at 256 entries EACH and sanitized through lib/permission-sanitize.mjs. A profile exceeding the cap is refused, not truncated: a silently truncated permission list is a security artifact, not a convenience.
